seo.title: Summarize PDF – Free AI PDF Summarizer, No Upload
seo.desc: Summarize a PDF in seconds: key sentences, key points and topics extracted on your device. Short, medium or detailed. Download TXT or Markdown. Free.
seo.compareTitle: {tool}: {brand} vs ChatPDF, Acrobat AI Assistant and Smallpdf
sections: Get the gist of a long report, paper, contract or e-book in seconds. The summarizer reads the whole PDF, ranks every sentence by how central it is to the document and gives you the most important ones in their original order, plus a list of key points and the main topics. Choose a short summary of five sentences, a medium one of about 10 % of the text or a detailed one of about 20 %.

steps: Drop the PDF (or tick Run OCR first for a scan).
Choose the summary length.
Press Summarize and read the key sentences, key points and topics.
Download the summary as .txt or Markdown.

table: The highest-ranked sentences in reading order
Short bullet list of the most informative statements
The most characteristic words and phrases of the document
Plain text or Markdown with headings, ready for notes apps

sections: *Short* is ideal for deciding whether a document is worth reading at all, or for an e-mail update. *Medium* (about a tenth of the text) captures the structure of most reports. *Detailed* keeps about a fifth – useful for study notes from a textbook chapter. For a very long book, summarise one chapter at a time using [Split PDF](/split-pdf/) or [Extract Pages](/extract-pdf-pages/) for better focus.

list: Remove cover pages, tables of contents and reference lists first – they add noise.
Summaries of well-structured prose (reports, articles, essays) are best; slide decks and forms have few full sentences.
Use the key topics to decide which section to read in full, then search it in [PDF Reader](/pdf-reader/).

sections: Turn the Markdown download into revision notes in Obsidian or Notion, paste key points into a meeting agenda, or build flashcards with the [PDF Question Generator](/pdf-question-generator/). For literature reviews, summarise each paper and keep the summaries alongside citations.

Fileopia's document AI does not send your PDF to a chatbot or a cloud model, and there is no large model to download. It uses proven, lightweight language-processing methods that run instantly in JavaScript: the text is split into sentences, every word is weighted by TF-IDF (how important it is in this document compared with ordinary language), and algorithms such as TextRank and BM25 – the ranking method behind many search engines – find the most central sentences or the passages that best match a question. Because everything is *extractive*, results are quoted from your document rather than generated, so the tool cannot invent facts, and every answer can be checked against the page it came from.

list: **Faithful:** output is always the document's own words, with no hallucinations.
**Fast and private:** a 200-page report is processed in seconds on a laptop, offline after loading.
**Language:** works best with English and other space-separated languages; OCR for scans is English.
**Not a chatbot:** it will not reason across pages, write new text, translate or answer questions whose answer is not stated in the document.
**Layout:** tables, footnotes and multi-column pages are read in text order, which can occasionally split a sentence.

sections: For a generative rewrite, paste the extracted summary into the AI assistant you already trust – you share only the summary, not the whole confidential file.

If the PDF is a scan or photo, it has no text layer and the tool will say that not enough text was found. Tick *Run OCR first (English)* and the pages are recognised on your device before analysis, or run [OCR PDF](/ocr-pdf/) separately to get a searchable copy you can keep.

Students revising textbooks and lecture notes, researchers triaging papers, lawyers and paralegals skimming contracts, analysts reading annual reports, HR teams reviewing policies and anyone handed a long PDF with little time. Because nothing is uploaded, it is suitable for documents covered by NDAs, client confidentiality or GDPR, where pasting into a public chatbot would not be allowed.

Everything happens inside your browser tab with pdf-lib and PDF.js. The PDF is read from your disk into memory, processed there and saved straight back to your device. It is never uploaded, stored or logged, and the tool keeps working offline once the page has loaded – which makes it suitable for contracts, medical records, HR files, bank statements and anything else you would not e-mail to a stranger.
compare: On-device, no upload to an AI service

seo.desc: Convert PDF to reflowable EPUB 3: headings, chapters, table of contents, header/footer removal and page images for scans. Free, no upload.
sections: PDFs have fixed pages, so on a phone or e-reader you zoom and scroll sideways. EPUB reflows text to fit the screen. This converter reads the PDF's text layer, rebuilds headings, paragraphs and lists, joins words hyphenated across lines, strips repeating headers, footers and page numbers, splits chapters and builds a real table of contents.

sections: Novels, reports, essays and text-heavy manuals from Word or InDesign convert best. Complex layouts – magazines, multi-column scientific papers, tables and maths – lose some structure because EPUB is a flowing format. Scanned PDFs have no text; run [OCR PDF](/ocr-pdf/) first, or include page images.
If the PDF has bookmarks, they become the EPUB's navigation; otherwise detected headings are used, so the reader's contents menu jumps straight to chapters.

Open the EPUB in Apple Books, Thorium Reader or Calibre's viewer and page through the first chapters. EPUB is the open e-book standard used by Apple Books, Google Play Books, Kobo, PocketBook, Tolino and most library apps; since 2022 Amazon's Send to Kindle also accepts EPUB and converts it for Kindle devices. An EPUB is a ZIP of XHTML chapters, CSS, images and a package file listing the reading order and table of contents, so text reflows to any screen size and readers can change the font and size. Files produced here are EPUB 3 with an EPUB 2 NCX table of contents for older readers. The files are validated against the structure EPUB readers expect – a mimetype entry, container.xml, a package document with metadata and spine, and a navigation document – so they open without warnings in strict apps such as Apple Books.
Reading on Kindle, phones and e-readers

sections: FictionBook (FB2) is an XML e-book format popular in Russia, Ukraine, Belarus and other Eastern European countries, and on many free-book libraries. Most readers outside that world – Apple Books, Google Play Books, Kindle via Send to Kindle, Kobo – need EPUB. This converter reads .fb2 and zipped .fb2.zip files and rebuilds them as clean EPUB 3 books.

steps: Drop the .fb2 or .fb2.zip file.

sections: FB2 stores a whole book in one XML file, with structure (sections, titles, poems, notes) rather than appearance, and images embedded as Base64. That makes it easy to convert faithfully: the converter maps the structure onto EPUB chapters and applies clean, readable styles.
FB2 files are usually UTF-8 or Windows-1251. The declared encoding is respected, so Cyrillic text converts correctly, and the book's language tag is copied so readers choose correct hyphenation.
On Kindle, send the EPUB with Send to Kindle; on Android use Play Books or ReadEra; on iOS use Books. For a printable copy, convert the EPUB with [EPUB to PDF](/epub-to-pdf/).
FB2 is the native format of large Russian-language libraries and of many public-domain classics shared online. Convert them once and keep the EPUB in your library app.

Converting a book you own for personal reading is usually fine; distributing it is not.

Everything happens inside your browser tab. Your books are read from your disk into memory, processed there and saved straight back to your device. Nothing is uploaded, stored or logged, there is no account, and the tool keeps working offline once the page has loaded – so it is safe for private, confidential and unreleased material.

seo.title: PDF to Speech – Read PDF Aloud Free, Text to Audio
seo.desc: Listen to any PDF, Word or text file read aloud with your device's voices. Highlights each sentence, speed and pitch, page range. Free, no upload.
sections: Listen to reports, articles, textbooks and e-mails while you commute, cook or rest your eyes. The tool extracts the text, cleans it (skipping headers and page numbers), and reads it aloud with the voices built into your phone, tablet or computer, highlighting each sentence as it goes. Click any sentence to jump there.

steps: Drop a PDF, Word or text file.
Optionally set the page range.
Choose a voice, speed and pitch.
Press Play; click sentences to jump; download the script if you like.

table: Microsoft voices, including natural online voices in Edge
Apple voices – download enhanced voices in Settings → Accessibility → Spoken Content

sections: Voice choice depends on your browser and system; more languages appear when you install them in your device settings.

list: People with dyslexia, low vision or reading fatigue.
Language learners who want to hear pronunciation.
Students reviewing notes on the go.
Writers proofreading their own drafts by ear – mistakes are easier to hear.

sections: Browsers' speech engines play through your speakers but do not hand the audio to web pages, so the tool cannot save an MP3. You can download the cleaned script (.txt, or timed captions in .srt style) and use it with a recorder or another app. For scans, run [OCR PDF](/ocr-pdf/) first.
Normal speech is about 150 words per minute. Many listeners comfortably follow 1.25–1.5× once used to a voice; slow down to 0.8× for technical material or a new language.

list: Use a text PDF, not a scan; OCR first if needed so words are recognised correctly.
Set a page range to skip covers, contents and references.
Headers, footers and page numbers are skipped, so they do not interrupt sentences.
Pick a voice that matches the document's language – an English voice reading French text sounds wrong.
On iPhone and Mac, download an *Enhanced* or *Premium* voice for much more natural speech.

sections: Listening while following the highlighted sentence – sometimes called bimodal reading – helps many people with dyslexia, ADHD or visual stress stay focused and remember more. Teachers can use it to give students an audio version of handouts without recording anything, and second-language learners can slow the speed down to follow pronunciation. Because the tool runs in the browser, it also works on school Chromebooks and locked-down office PCs where installing software is not allowed.

Word documents (.docx) and plain text files are read the same way. For web articles, save the page as PDF from the browser's print dialog first, or paste the text into [Text to Speech](/text-to-speech/).

On a phone, keep the browser tab open and the screen on while listening; some mobile browsers pause speech when the screen locks or you switch apps. For long documents, read one chapter at a time using the page range, and note the page number where you stopped so you can resume later. Wired or Bluetooth headphones work exactly like any other audio. Battery use is low because speech is generated by the operating system rather than streamed from a server, and no mobile data is used once the page has loaded.

Everything happens inside your browser tab. Your documents are read from your disk into memory, processed there and saved straight back to your device. Nothing is uploaded, stored or logged, there is no account, and the tool keeps working offline once the page has loaded – so it is safe for private, confidential and unreleased material.
